You will recall that there was a matter raised by my colleague, Mr. Zecevic the other day regarding notification of resumption of rights of people in this sort of situation, and I just wanted to establish whether his enforcement of his rights is something that he has pursued or whether it's something that he has been notified of and that's really what I'm concerned about.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: In fact, Witness, what I'll ask you is this: the recent moves that you've made to clean out your apartment, get it ready and find a buyer for it and so on, is that something that you've done of your own initiative or is it something that you have been informed you can do by authorities in the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed by the authorities in the Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: What were you told?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: That if I did not intend to go back, that's what I learned in the Ministry for Refugees and Displaced Persons, that I could either rent or sell my apartment. They gave me the two options. The third option was for me to return to Samac.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: When were you told of this?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was -- I heard that for two years and it was actually two years that it took me to gain this right for my apartment because I had to run around and chase all the paperwork, and things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the witness said that he went to ministry and it's not appears in his answer in the transcript. Thank you. MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Did you attend a ministry in the Republika Srpska in pursuit of your rights?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Which of the authorities in the Republika Srpska told you about your rights in respect of your apartment?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was informed by the head of the ministry, Marinko Tirnanic from Jajce and Miroslav Zoranovic from Samac they told me that, and actually I addressed them regarding this issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: That's what I want to know. Who approached who first? What I want to know is was it the authorities of the Republika Srpska who raised the issue or did you go and raise the issue with them? That's what I want to know?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I went there and I approached them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Thank you. Apart from your apartment and your personal possessions, did you have any other property that you lost? I refer to, for example, the tools of your trade, a vehicle, things like that.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just my tools, the tools that I had, because I worked. I lost that. But that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Any vehicles?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: MR. DI FAZIO:

utterances.speaker: MR. DI
utterances.text: Just to wrap it up, just one last question, Witness. You've already told us that the furniture and your memorabilia and so on went missing from the apartment, what about fixtures in the apartment, things like radiators, stuff that's attached, actually fixed into the apartment. Did you suffer any loss there?

utterances.speaker: WITNESS M [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not have any radiators, and as regards the water and electricity fittings, everything had been taken out. The apartment was stripped. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, I don't think there's any other topic that I can usefully pursue today and so I'd like to, with the Chamber's permission, to bring a halt to my examination-in-chief at this stage and deal with the remaining issue hopefully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Pending the decision on the motion. MR. DI FAZIO: Pending the decision, of course, in January. I don't want to say that I have absolutely no further questions on the issue of property. It may be that after a review of the transcript, I might have a few more but --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The point is you haven't completed your examination-in-chief. MR. DI FAZIO: Essentially, yes. I just wanted to reserve my rights in that respect.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So Witness, the Prosecution will call you, they will notify you when to come so they can complete their examination and also, the Defence counsel can have the opportunity to cross-examine you and the Judges, of course, if they wish to put any more questions. For the time being, you will be released and you are free to go until you receive notification from the Prosecution as to when you should give evidence to the Tribunal. Thank you. You will be led out of the courtroom by the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before we rise, there are a few matters that the Trial Chamber would like to deal with and perhaps also ask the parties if there are any matters they want to discuss. There was a problem, a report that the Trial Chamber received from counsel for the Defence regarding contacts between witnesses of the Prosecution right at the beginning of these proceedings, and the Trial Chamber did inform the Victims and Witnesses Unit to seek their response and also to find out how the witnesses were being looked after in The Hague. The position with the Victims and Witnesses Unit is that they are not attached to the Prosecution or to the Defence. They are an independent unit under the office of the Registrar and their duties include looking after all the witnesses who are summoned to come and give evidence before the Tribunal. These are Prosecution witnesses, witnesses of the Court, and Defence witnesses alike. Among their duties is counselling for the witnesses, to see that the witnesses are comfortable, they understand what is involved in giving evidence, they have the facilities they need. If they are on medication or if there are any other special requirements that they need for their health and their well-being, all those matters are attended to. And some of the officials of the Victims and Witnesses Unit actually accompany the witnesses to the hotels or wherever they are being -- they have accommodation and also accompany them to the Tribunal when they come to give evidence or attend to them even when they have to see a doctor. Now, during those contacts, there is nothing to stop a witness and the official from the Victims and Witnesses Unit to discuss how they fared in the courtroom while giving evidence, what their fears are, and that sort of thing. The duty of the official is they understand what their obligations are and they are at ease. If there is any problem, then they will notify either the Prosecution in the event of a Prosecution witness or the Defence counsel in the event of a Defence witness as to what should be done because there have been incidences in the past when we have had witnesses who have either fallen ill or have become scared to continue and activities have been undertaken by the unit to notify the relevant parties including the Trial Chamber so that action can be taken. There is nothing to stop a witness who requires a digestive at any time of the day to take that, and perhaps even invite any official from the Victims and Witnesses Unit to accompany him or accompany her. There is absolutely nothing wrong with that. As for accommodation, the Victims and Witnesses Unit do try to keep witnesses of a given case in one hotel for ease of transport and also to be able to look after them. And in a situation where you have trials including appeals going on more or less at various times or at the same time, they become quite overloaded so that it is not possible for each witness to have his or her own personal attendant from the unit so they normally do it -- they look after the witnesses as a group. So it's not uncommon for witnesses to meet and greet each other, but they do make sure they warn them never to discuss the evidence that they have given in court or that they are going to give in the Tribunal. After these complaints were raised, the Trial Chamber waited to see whether or not this problem would continue and nothing has been reported since so the Trial Chamber is satisfied that there was nothing untoward in the incidents that were reported and that the Victims and Witnesses Unit did comply with their duties as they were required to do. Any other matters before we rise formally? The Defence? Or the Prosecution first, yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, a matter that I want to attend to is this, just the order of the day when we resume in January. I raised the other day the issue of how we continue on the 14th when we resume. I assume that we will continue with the examination-in-chief of this witness.

If the decision does go in favour of the Prosecution and I do -- and I'm then poised, ready to finish off his examination-in-chief, would the Chamber expect me to do that before calling any further evidence on the Variant A and B witnesses?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It would be preferable so that the cross-examination then can follow on -- MR. DI FAZIO: Right. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- and then the witness can be released once and for all. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Is this understanding correct: If the decision is in favour of the Prosecution, I would then continue my examination-in-chief, he would then be cross-examined, finish the witness entirely, and then interpose the evidence relating to the Variant A and B --

utterances.text: Before the next full witness. And also, remember that we still have another witness who is to be cross-examined. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes, that's right. Exactly. That witness as well. Would the Chamber prefer that we finish off his cross-examination as well before the Variant A and B witnesses are called? It's a question of scheduling witnesses and so on. I need an indication from that so that my colleagues can prepare for that evidence and we can make sure that witnesses are produced seamlessly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think the details of the planning can be left to the Prosecution, because you will receive the decision of the Chamber and you'll plan accordingly. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down for the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You'll receive the decision of the Chamber and you're going to plan accordingly. The point which is here is that Witness M has not yet finished examination, and then we'll proceed after that to cross-examination. We have another witness who was -- who completed examination-in-chief -- MR. DI FAZIO: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: -- who has yet to come for cross-examination. As for Variant A and B, it can be rescheduled according to your preference. The Defence have enough notice that this witness for Variant A and B most likely will come in January or early next year, so I'm sure that they will have prepared themselves for cross-examination, because they were given the relevant documents. MR. DI FAZIO: Thank you. Well, in that case, can I announce to the Chamber, and for the benefit of my learned friends, that if the decision is in favour of the Prosecution, then I am minded to do this: Finish my examination-in-chief of this witness, have his cross-examination and his re-examination, finish him completely. utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Just briefly, I wanted to respond to this victims and witnesses issue. And let me just say, I appreciate the Chamber looking into the matters.
